name: Tuna & Oat Crunch Biscuits
description: Crisp little tuna biscuits with four ingredients and no salt. An occasional treat, not a meal.
body: *Four ingredients, one bowl, twenty-five minutes. The smell will bring every cat in the building.*

![Homemade heart-shaped cat biscuits cooling on baking paper next to a storage jar](https://storage.googleapis.com/yucat-d8fb5.firebasestorage.app/recipes/tuna-oat-crunch-biscuits.jpeg)
*Aim for small, firm biscuits that snap rather than bend. Photo by Monika Animallama, [CC BY 2.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/).*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Makes** | About 40 small biscuits |
| **Prep / Bake** | 10 min / 15 min |
| **Difficulty** | Easy |
| **Keeps** | 5 days airtight, 6 weeks frozen |
## Ingredients

- **140 g canned tuna in spring water**, thoroughly drained
- **120 g oat flour** — or porridge oats blitzed fine
- **1 medium egg**
- **1 tbsp sunflower or olive oil**
- **1–2 tbsp water**, only if needed
> **Nothing else goes in.** No salt, garlic, onion powder, stock cube or cheese. Onion and garlic damage feline red blood cells. Use tuna in spring water, never brine or oil.
## Method

1. **Heat the oven** to 180 °C (160 °C fan) and line a tray with baking paper.
2. **Drain the tuna hard**, pressing it against a sieve. Wet tuna gives a paste that will not hold a shape.
3. **Mash it fine** with a fork, leaving no large flakes.
4. **Mix in the egg and oil** to a thick paste.
5. **Work in the oat flour** a third at a time, until the dough leaves the bowl clean. Add water only if it will not come together.
6. **Roll to 5 mm** between two sheets of baking paper. Thicker biscuits stay chewy inside and spoil faster.
7. **Cut into 1 cm squares.** Cat treats should be genuinely tiny.
8. **Bake 12–15 minutes**, until the edges are golden and the tops feel dry.
9. **Cool completely on a rack** — they crisp as they cool.
## Portioning
Treats should stay under **10% of daily calories**. Reduce the main meal slightly on days you use them; this is where home-baking quietly makes cats fat.

| Cat weight | Treat allowance | Biscuits per day |
|---|---|---|
| 3 kg | 16 kcal | 2–3 |
| 4 kg | 20 kcal | 3–4 |
| 5–6 kg | 24–27 kcal | 4–5 |
## Storage

![Baked cat biscuits cooling on parchment beside a filled glass jar](https://storage.googleapis.com/yucat-d8fb5.firebasestorage.app/recipes/tuna-oat-crunch-biscuits-b1.jpeg)
*Cool them fully before jarring. Trapped steam turns a crisp biscuit soft overnight. Photo by Monika Animallama, [CC BY 2.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/).*

- **Airtight jar:** 5 days · **Fridge:** 2 weeks · **Freezer:** 6 weeks
- Freeze flat on a tray first, then bag
- No preservatives means no shortcuts — if they smell sour, bin them
## Variations

- **Salmon:** tinned salmon in water, bones removed
- **Chicken:** 150 g plain poached chicken, blitzed, plus an extra tbsp water
- **Harder crunch:** roll to 8 mm and bake 5 minutes longer
## Cautions

- **Fish is a treat, not a staple.** Two or three treat days a week is plenty.
- **Introduce one new food at a time** so you can spot a reaction.
- **Skip** for cats with a fish allergy; check with your vet first for kidney disease, pancreatitis or diabetes.
- **Break biscuits in half** for greedy eaters.
*Home-made treats are complementary food. They are not complete and balanced and should never replace a cat's main diet.*
*Photographs by Monika Animallama, used under [CC BY 2.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/).*

name: Chicken & Pumpkin Lick Pâté
description: A smooth, spoonable pâté of poached chicken and pumpkin. Gentle on digestion and useful for hiding medication.
body: *Soft and spoonable — for fussy eaters, older cats, and anyone who has tried to give a cat a tablet.*

![A smooth orange puree served in two bowls](https://storage.googleapis.com/yucat-d8fb5.firebasestorage.app/recipes/chicken-pumpkin-lick-pate.jpeg)
*The texture to aim for: smooth enough to fall off a spoon, thick enough to hold its shape. Serve yours plain, without the garnish shown here.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Makes** | 8 servings of 1 tbsp |
| **Prep / Cook** | 10 min / 20 min |
| **Difficulty** | Easy |
| **Keeps** | 3 days chilled, 1 month frozen |
## Why it earns its place

- **Texture** — suits cats with dental pain or missing teeth
- **Moisture** — carries a lot of water into a species that drinks badly
- **Camouflage** — the most reliable way to hide a crushed tablet, if your vet confirms the drug may be given with food
## Ingredients

- **200 g chicken breast**, skinless and boneless
- **2 tbsp plain pumpkin purée** — 100% pumpkin
- **3–4 tbsp of the cooking water**, reserved
- **1 tsp salmon or sardine oil** *(optional)*

> **Pie filling is not purée.** It contains sugar and often nutmeg, which is toxic to cats. The tin must list pumpkin and nothing else. Never use chicken from a roast dinner — cooking fat, salt, onion and garlic are all problems, and the last two are toxic.
## Method

1. **Poach the chicken** in unsalted water at a gentle simmer for 15–18 minutes, until no pink remains.
2. **Reserve 4 tbsp of the cooking water.** This is your flavour and moisture — never a stock cube.
3. **Cool completely.** Cats reject food above body temperature, and scalding is a real risk.
4. **Check for bone and cartilage** with your fingers before blending.
5. **Blend the chicken** with 2 tbsp of the cooking water to a coarse paste.
6. **Add the pumpkin** and blend smooth.
7. **Adjust with the remaining water**, a spoon at a time, until it falls slowly off a spoon.
8. **Stir the oil through** at the end. Do not blend it — heat and blades degrade omega-3s.
## Serving

![A cat eating from a bowl](https://storage.googleapis.com/yucat-d8fb5.firebasestorage.app/articles/why-cats-cannot-be-vegetarian-b1.jpeg)
*A wide, shallow dish keeps the whiskers out of the food.*
Start with **one teaspoon** to test tolerance, then build to a tablespoon.

| Cat weight | Treat allowance | Pâté per day |
|---|---|---|
| 3 kg | 16 kcal | 1 tsp |
| 4 kg | 20 kcal | 1½ tsp |
| 5 kg | 24 kcal | 1 tbsp |
## Storage

- **Fridge:** 3 days sealed · **Freezer:** 1 month, frozen in an ice-cube tray then bagged
- **Thaw overnight in the fridge** — never on the counter, never in a microwave, which creates burning hot spots
## Variations

- **Turkey** instead of chicken, identical method
- **Extra hydration:** loosen with more cooking water into a gravy
- **Sensitive stomach:** leave out the oil and halve the pumpkin
## Cautions

- **This is not a complete meal.** No taurine, no calcium balance, no vitamin premix. Cats fed plain chicken as a staple develop serious deficiencies.
- **More pumpkin is not better** — too much causes loose stools.
- **Ask your vet before using it to hide medication**, and before feeding it to cats with diabetes, kidney disease or pancreatitis.
- **Introduce over three or four days** for a sensitive stomach.
*Home-made recipes are treats and supplements to a complete, balanced diet.*

name: Frozen Salmon Broth Cubes
description: Salmon-scented ice cubes that get water into a cat that refuses to drink. Fifteen minutes of work, then the freezer does the rest.
body: *A hydration trick disguised as a treat — for hot weather, fussy drinkers and cats on dry food.*

![Heart-shaped cubes set in a silicone tray, with several turned out alongside](https://storage.googleapis.com/yucat-d8fb5.firebasestorage.app/recipes/frozen-salmon-broth-cubes.jpeg)
*A small silicone tray gives the right portion size. Turn the cubes out once solid and bag them.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Makes** | 12–14 cubes |
| **Active time** | 15 minutes |
| **Freezing** | 4 hours minimum |
| **Keeps** | 2 months frozen |
## The problem this solves

Cats descend from desert animals and have a famously weak thirst drive. Wild prey is about **70% water**, so a cat barely needs to drink. On dry food that water is simply absent, and chronic mild dehydration contributes to **urinary crystals, cystitis and kidney strain**.
> A cat on wet food takes in roughly three to four times more water per day than the same cat on kibble alone.
You cannot make a cat drink. You can make water more interesting.
## Ingredients

- **100 g salmon fillet**, skinless and boneless — or tinned salmon in spring water
- **400 ml water**, unsalted
- **1 tbsp plain pumpkin purée** *(optional, for body)*
> **No stock cubes, no bouillon, no seasoning.** Commercial stock is loaded with salt and almost always contains onion.
## Method

1. **Simmer the salmon** gently in the 400 ml of water for 10 minutes, until opaque throughout.
2. **Lift the fish out** and cool both fish and liquid completely.
3. **Check the fillet obsessively for bones**, running a finger along the grain. Salmon pin bones are fine and easy to miss.
4. **Strain the broth** through a fine sieve to catch stray bone or skin.
5. **Blend a third of the salmon** back into the broth for aroma and body. Keep the rest for another recipe.
6. **Whisk in the pumpkin** if using — it stops the cubes shattering into slivers.
7. **Pour into a tray and freeze** at least 4 hours, then transfer to a labelled freezer bag.
## Three ways to serve

- **In the water bowl.** One cube flavours and chills the water without a full treat's calories. This is the daily version.
- **On a plate.** A lick-and-chase treat on a hot day. Expect it to be batted across the kitchen first.
- **Melted as a topper.** Thaw one over dry food to add moisture and tempt an inappetent cat.
Start with **one cube a day** — the 10%-of-daily-calories rule applies here too.
## Storage

- **Freezer:** 2 months sealed · **Thawed broth:** 2 days in the fridge, then discard
- **Never refreeze** a thawed cube
- **Label the bag with the date.** Unlabelled homemade cat food becomes a mystery within a fortnight.
## Variations

- **Chicken** poaching liquid, same method — milder and often better tolerated
- **Tuna** in spring water for a stronger smell
- **Plain water cubes** for cats that already drink well and just like the game
## Cautions

- **Never use commercial stock.** Onion, garlic and salt are standard, and the first two are toxic.
- **Bones are the real risk.** Strain the liquid and check the flesh twice.
- **Thaw slightly** for cats with dental disease or hard ice-crunchers.
- **Fish two or three times a week at most** — cats fixate on it to the exclusion of balanced food.
- **Check with your vet** for cats with kidney disease or on a prescription diet.
*A treat, not a meal. Complementary food does not replace a complete and balanced diet.*

name: Chicken Liver Bites
description: Intensely aromatic liver and oat bites. Powerful training treats, strictly rationed for vitamin A.
body: *The most persuasive treat in this collection, and the one with the firmest limit on it.*

![Raw chicken on a cutting board](https://storage.googleapis.com/yucat-d8fb5.firebasestorage.app/recipes/chicken-liver-bites.jpeg)
*Liver is nutrient-dense to the point where the dose genuinely matters.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Makes** | About 50 tiny bites |
| **Prep / Bake** | 12 min / 18 min |
| **Difficulty** | Easy |
| **Keeps** | 4 days chilled, 6 weeks frozen |
## Ingredients

- **150 g chicken liver**, trimmed
- **100 g oat flour**
- **1 medium egg**
- **1 tbsp of the cooking water**
> **Nothing else.** No salt, onion, garlic or seasoning of any kind.
## Method

1. **Simmer the liver** in unsalted water for 8 minutes, until firm and no longer bloody inside.
2. **Reserve a tablespoon of the water** and cool everything completely.
3. **Blend the liver** to a smooth paste.
4. **Beat in the egg**, then work in the oat flour to a stiff dough.
5. **Heat the oven** to 180 °C (160 °C fan) and line a tray.
6. **Roll to 4 mm** and cut into pieces no bigger than **5 mm square**. These are deliberately minuscule.
7. **Bake 15–18 minutes** until dry and firm, then cool fully on a rack.
## Portioning — read this part
Liver is extremely rich in **preformed vitamin A**, which cats store rather than excrete. Long-term excess causes **hypervitaminosis A**, producing painful bony growths along the spine and joints.

| Cat weight | Maximum per day | Days per week |
|---|---|---|
| 3–4 kg | 2 bites | 2 |
| 5–6 kg | 3 bites | 2 |
Treat this as a **twice-weekly training treat**, not a daily snack. The tiny size is the safety mechanism.
## Storage

- **Fridge:** 4 days in a sealed jar · **Freezer:** 6 weeks
- Liver treats spoil faster than fish or chicken ones — when in doubt, discard
## Variations

- **Turkey liver** instead of chicken, same quantities
- **Softer texture** for older cats: bake 12 minutes and keep refrigerated
- **Extra binding** if the dough is sticky: another tablespoon of oat flour
## Cautions

- **Vitamin A is the whole issue.** Stick to the table above and do not improvise upward.
- **Not for cats already on a liver-containing diet** without asking your vet.
- **Avoid entirely** for pregnant cats — excess vitamin A causes birth defects.
- **Skip** for cats with liver disease or on a restricted diet.
*A treat, not a meal. Complementary food does not replace a complete and balanced diet.*

name: Salmon & Catnip Cookies
description: Crisp salmon cookies with dried catnip stirred through. The most reliably accepted treat for fussy cats.
body: *Two of the strongest feline attractants in one biscuit.*

![Round cookies cooling on a white surface](https://storage.googleapis.com/yucat-d8fb5.firebasestorage.app/recipes/salmon-catnip-cookies.jpeg)
*Small, flat and evenly baked. Size is what keeps the calories honest.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Makes** | About 40 cookies |
| **Prep / Bake** | 10 min / 15 min |
| **Difficulty** | Easy |
| **Keeps** | 5 days airtight, 6 weeks frozen |
## Ingredients

- **150 g tinned salmon in spring water**, drained, bones removed
- **120 g oat or brown rice flour**
- **1 medium egg**
- **1 tsp dried catnip**
- **1 tbsp water**, if needed
> Salmon in **spring water**, never brine or oil. Check for and remove the soft vertebrae in tinned salmon, even though they are edible — they make the texture gritty.
## Method

1. **Heat the oven** to 180 °C (160 °C fan) and line a tray.
2. **Drain the salmon hard** and mash it completely smooth.
3. **Mix in the egg**, then the catnip.
4. **Add the flour** gradually to a firm, non-sticky dough.
5. **Roll to 5 mm** between baking paper and cut into 1 cm rounds or squares.
6. **Bake 12–15 minutes** until the edges colour and the tops feel dry.
7. **Cool completely** on a rack before storing.
## About the catnip
Roughly **two thirds of cats** respond to catnip; the trait is inherited, and kittens under about three months rarely react at all.
If your cat is a non-responder, the cookies still work — salmon carries them on its own. **Silvervine** is a good alternative and many catnip-immune cats respond to it instead.
## Portioning

| Cat weight | Treat allowance | Cookies per day |
|---|---|---|
| 3 kg | 16 kcal | 2–3 |
| 4 kg | 20 kcal | 3–4 |
| 5–6 kg | 24–27 kcal | 4–5 |
## Storage

- **Airtight jar:** 5 days · **Fridge:** 2 weeks · **Freezer:** 6 weeks
- Cool completely first, or trapped steam softens them overnight
## Variations

- **Silvervine** in place of catnip for non-responders
- **Tuna** in spring water instead of salmon
- **Dental version:** roll to 8 mm and bake 5 minutes longer
## Cautions

- **Fish two or three times a week at most.** Cats fixate on it easily.
- **Bones out.** Check the drained salmon by hand.
- **Skip** for cats with a fish allergy.
- **Catnip in excess** occasionally causes mild vomiting — one teaspoon in the whole batch is plenty.
*A treat, not a meal. Complementary food does not replace a complete and balanced diet.*

name: Sardine Crunch Treats
description: Omega-rich sardine biscuits with a firm snap. Strong-smelling, which is the point for older cats.
body: *Sardines are small, oily, sustainable and packed with omega-3. Cats can smell them from another floor.*

![An open tin of sardines](https://storage.googleapis.com/yucat-d8fb5.firebasestorage.app/recipes/sardine-crunch-treats.jpeg)
*Sardines in spring water. The soft bones are edible and blend away completely.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Makes** | About 35 treats |
| **Prep / Bake** | 10 min / 16 min |
| **Difficulty** | Easy |
| **Keeps** | 4 days airtight, 6 weeks frozen |
## Ingredients

- **120 g tinned sardines in spring water**, drained
- **130 g oat flour**
- **1 medium egg**
- **1–2 tbsp water**, if needed
No added oil in this one. Sardines bring plenty of their own.
> **Spring water only.** Sardines in brine carry far too much salt, and those in oil make a greasy dough that will not crisp.
## Method

1. **Heat the oven** to 180 °C (160 °C fan) and line a tray.
2. **Drain the sardines thoroughly**, pressing them against a sieve.
3. **Mash completely**, bones included — they are soft, edible and a good calcium source.
4. **Beat in the egg.**
5. **Work in the flour** to a firm dough, adding water only if it will not hold together.
6. **Roll to 5 mm** and cut into 1 cm pieces.
7. **Bake 14–16 minutes**, then cool completely on a rack.
## Why sardines

- **Omega-3 fatty acids** support skin, coat and joint comfort
- **Naturally low in mercury**, unlike tuna, because they are small and short-lived
- **Soft edible bones** add calcium that fillet fish does not
- **Aroma**, which matters enormously for older cats whose sense of smell has faded
## Portioning

| Cat weight | Treat allowance | Treats per day |
|---|---|---|
| 3 kg | 16 kcal | 2 |
| 4 kg | 20 kcal | 3 |
| 5–6 kg | 24–27 kcal | 3–4 |
Sardines are calorie-dense, so these run slightly smaller than the tuna biscuits.
## Storage

- **Airtight jar:** 4 days · **Fridge:** 10 days · **Freezer:** 6 weeks
- Oily treats go rancid faster. Refrigerate in warm weather.
## Variations

- **Mackerel** in spring water, same method
- **Softer texture** for dental patients: bake 11 minutes and keep chilled
- **Joint support version:** add 1 tsp of plain ground flaxseed to the dough
## Cautions

- **Two or three fish days a week at most.** Oily fish fed daily can deplete vitamin E.
- **Never raw sardines** in quantity — some raw fish contains thiaminase, which destroys vitamin B1.
- **Skip** for cats with a fish allergy or on a restricted-phosphorus renal diet.
- **Check the tin.** Some sardines are packed with tomato or oil and are unsuitable.
*A treat, not a meal. Complementary food does not replace a complete and balanced diet.*

name: Turkey & Cranberry Biscuits
description: Lean turkey biscuits with a little unsweetened cranberry. A mild, low-fat treat.
body: *Lean, mild and low in fat — a useful treat for cats that need to watch their weight.*

![A tray of freshly baked biscuits](https://storage.googleapis.com/yucat-d8fb5.firebasestorage.app/recipes/turkey-and-cranberry-biscuits.jpeg)
*Turkey breast is one of the leanest proteins you can put in a treat.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Makes** | About 40 biscuits |
| **Prep / Bake** | 15 min / 15 min |
| **Difficulty** | Easy |
| **Keeps** | 5 days airtight, 6 weeks frozen |
## Ingredients

- **200 g turkey breast**, skinless and boneless
- **120 g oat flour**
- **1 medium egg**
- **1 tbsp unsweetened dried cranberry**, finely chopped
- **2 tbsp of the cooking water**

> **Unsweetened cranberry only.** Standard dried cranberries are sweetened, often heavily, and sometimes contain other dried fruit. Read the packet, and if in doubt leave it out — the biscuits work without it.
## Method

1. **Poach the turkey** in unsalted water for 15 minutes, until cooked through.
2. **Reserve 2 tbsp of the cooking water**, then cool everything completely.
3. **Blend the turkey** to a fine paste with the reserved water.
4. **Mix in the egg** and the chopped cranberry.
5. **Work in the oat flour** to a firm dough.
6. **Heat the oven** to 180 °C (160 °C fan), line a tray, and roll the dough to 5 mm.
7. **Cut into 1 cm pieces** and bake 13–15 minutes until dry and lightly golden.
8. **Cool completely** before storing.
## An honest note on cranberry

Cranberry is widely marketed for feline urinary health. The evidence in cats is **weak** — most of it is extrapolated from human studies of a different type of urinary infection, and feline urinary disease is usually sterile inflammation rather than bacterial.

It is included here as a mild, safe flavour, not as a treatment. **The genuinely effective urinary measure is water intake**, which is why the frozen broth cubes in this collection matter more than this ingredient does.
## Portioning

| Cat weight | Treat allowance | Biscuits per day |
|---|---|---|
| 3 kg | 16 kcal | 3 |
| 4 kg | 20 kcal | 4 |
| 5–6 kg | 24–27 kcal | 4–5 |
Lean turkey makes these lower in calories than the fish biscuits, so the count runs slightly higher.
## Storage
- **Airtight jar:** 5 days · **Fridge:** 2 weeks · **Freezer:** 6 weeks
## Variations

- **Plain turkey**, cranberry omitted — genuinely just as good
- **Chicken breast** instead of turkey
- **Blueberry** in place of cranberry, fresh and finely chopped
## Cautions

- **Never use raisins, sultanas or grapes** as a substitute. They are linked to kidney failure in pets.
- **Cranberry acidifies urine.** Cats with a history of **calcium oxalate** stones should avoid it — ask your vet, since acidification helps one stone type and worsens another.
- **Skip the fruit entirely** for diabetic cats.
- **Turkey from a roast dinner is not suitable** — the fat, salt, onion and garlic are all problems.
*A treat, not a meal. Complementary food does not replace a complete and balanced diet.*

name: Chicken & Parsley Crisps
description: Thin, very crisp chicken wafers with a little flat-leaf parsley. Freshens breath a little and crunches a lot.
body: *Rolled thinner than the other biscuits and baked longer, for a genuine snap.*

![Biscuits on a baking sheet](https://storage.googleapis.com/yucat-d8fb5.firebasestorage.app/recipes/chicken-and-parsley-crisps.jpeg)
*Thin and dry is what makes these crisp rather than chewy.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Makes** | About 45 crisps |
| **Prep / Bake** | 15 min / 20 min |
| **Difficulty** | Easy |
| **Keeps** | 7 days airtight, 6 weeks frozen |
## Ingredients

- **200 g chicken breast**, skinless and boneless
- **110 g oat flour**
- **1 medium egg white** *(the yolk makes them softer)*
- **1 tsp fresh flat-leaf parsley**, very finely chopped
- **2 tbsp of the cooking water**

> **Flat-leaf parsley in small amounts only.** Curly parsley is fine too. **Spring parsley is not** — it is a different plant and is toxic to cats. A teaspoon across the whole batch is the right dose.
## Method

1. **Poach the chicken** in unsalted water for 15–18 minutes until cooked through.
2. **Reserve 2 tbsp of the water** and cool everything completely.
3. **Blend the chicken** with the reserved water to a smooth paste.
4. **Mix in the egg white** and the parsley.
5. **Work in the flour** to a firm dough.
6. **Heat the oven** to 170 °C (150 °C fan) — lower than the other recipes, so they dry rather than brown.
7. **Roll to 3 mm**, thinner than you think is sensible, between two sheets of baking paper.
8. **Cut into 1 cm squares** and bake **18–20 minutes**.
9. **Turn the oven off and leave them inside** for 10 minutes to finish drying. Cool completely.
## Why thin matters
A crisp treat has a mild abrasive effect at the tooth surface, and it stores far better because there is no moisture left inside. Thicker biscuits stay chewy in the middle and go off within days.
**This is not a substitute for brushing.** No treat is. Brushing is the only measure with strong evidence behind it, and these are a small extra.
## Portioning

| Cat weight | Treat allowance | Crisps per day |
|---|---|---|
| 3 kg | 16 kcal | 3–4 |
| 4 kg | 20 kcal | 4–5 |
| 5–6 kg | 24–27 kcal | 5–6 |
## Storage

- **Airtight jar:** 7 days, the longest in this collection, because they are properly dry
- **Freezer:** 6 weeks
- If they lose their snap, refresh for 5 minutes in a 150 °C oven and cool again
## Variations

- **Turkey** instead of chicken
- **Parsley-free**, which suits cats on restricted diets and tastes no different to them
- **Extra crunch:** roll to 2 mm and drop the bake to 16 minutes so they do not burn
## Cautions

- **Parsley in quantity is not safe.** Keep to the stated teaspoon; large amounts can cause photosensitivity.
- **Avoid entirely** for pregnant cats and those with kidney disease.
- **Never spring parsley**, which is a toxic look-alike.
- **Break in half** for cats with dental disease, or skip this recipe for them and use the pâté instead.
*A treat, not a meal. Complementary food does not replace a complete and balanced diet.*

name: Simple Poached Chicken Dinner
description: Plain poached chicken with its own cooking liquid. A bland, tempting dish for a cat that has gone off its food.
body: *The dish to make when a cat is recovering, off its food, or being reintroduced to eating.*

![Two raw chicken breasts in a bowl](https://storage.googleapis.com/yucat-d8fb5.firebasestorage.app/recipes/simple-poached-chicken-dinner.jpeg)
*Plain breast, unsalted water, nothing else.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Makes** | 3–4 servings |
| **Prep / Cook** | 5 min / 20 min |
| **Difficulty** | Easy |
| **Keeps** | 3 days chilled, 1 month frozen |
## Read this first

This is **not a complete diet**. It has no taurine supplement, no calcium-to-phosphorus balance and no vitamin premix. Fed as a cat's main food it causes serious deficiencies within weeks, including **taurine-linked blindness and heart disease**.
Use it as a short-term appetite bridge of a few days, then return to complete food. If a cat needs a home-prepared diet longer than that, it must be formulated by a **veterinary nutritionist**.
## Ingredients

- **250 g chicken breast**, skinless and boneless
- **Unsalted water** to cover
That is the entire list.
## Method

1. **Place the chicken in a small pan** and cover with cold unsalted water by about 2 cm.
2. **Bring to a bare simmer**, never a rolling boil, which toughens the meat.
3. **Cook 18–20 minutes**, until no pink remains at the thickest point.
4. **Keep all the cooking liquid.** Taurine leaches into it during cooking, and pouring it away removes a nutrient the cat specifically needs.
5. **Cool completely** — cats reject food above body temperature and scalding is a genuine risk.
6. **Check by hand for cartilage**, then shred finely along the grain.
7. **Moisten generously** with the cooking liquid before serving.
## Serving
Serve at room temperature on a **wide, shallow plate**. Deep bowls press on the whiskers and some cats will not eat from them.

| Cat weight | As a full meal replacement | As a topper |
|---|---|---|
| 3 kg | 60 g plus liquid | 1 tsp |
| 4 kg | 80 g plus liquid | 1½ tsp |
| 5–6 kg | 100 g plus liquid | 1 tbsp |
**Maximum three consecutive days** as a full replacement, then back to complete food.
## Storage

- **Fridge:** 3 days sealed · **Freezer:** 1 month in portions
- Freeze the liquid with the meat, not separately
- **Thaw in the fridge**, never in a microwave, which creates burning hot spots
## Variations

- **Turkey breast**, identical method
- **White fish** — cod or haddock — poached 8 minutes instead
- **Extra moisture** for a dehydrated cat: serve as a soup rather than shredded meat
## Cautions

- **Never feed long term.** Three days is the limit without veterinary guidance.
- **A cat that will not eat for 24 hours needs a vet**, not more recipes. Cats develop **hepatic lipidosis** after short fasts.
- **No bones, skin, salt, oil, onion or garlic.**
- **Ask your vet first** for cats with kidney disease or pancreatitis.
*Complementary food only. This recipe is a short-term appetite aid, not a diet.*

name: Turkey & Rice Recovery Meal
description: A bland, gentle meal for a cat with an upset stomach. Short-term use, on veterinary advice.
body: *The classic bland diet, adapted for a carnivore — which means far more meat than the dog version.*

![Cooked chicken pieces in a dish](https://storage.googleapis.com/yucat-d8fb5.firebasestorage.app/recipes/turkey-and-rice-recovery-meal.jpeg)
*Three parts meat to one part rice, not the other way round.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Makes** | 4 servings |
| **Prep / Cook** | 10 min / 25 min |
| **Difficulty** | Easy |
| **Keeps** | 3 days chilled, 1 month frozen |
## When to use it, and when not to
Bland diets are for **mild, self-limiting digestive upset**, and always with your vet's agreement first.

**Call the vet before cooking anything** if there is blood in the stool or vomit, repeated vomiting, lethargy, a painful abdomen, no food for 24 hours, or if the cat is a kitten, elderly or has existing disease.
> Vomiting and diarrhoea dehydrate a cat quickly. A bland meal is supportive care, not treatment.
## Ingredients

- **250 g turkey breast**, skinless and boneless
- **80 g white rice**, cooked plain — white, not brown, which is harder to digest
- **Unsalted water** to cook both
Roughly **three parts meat to one part rice** by cooked weight. Cats are carnivores; the dog ratio of mostly rice is wrong for them.
## Method

1. **Cook the rice** in unsalted water until soft — a little overcooked is better here.
2. **Poach the turkey** separately in unsalted water for 18 minutes.
3. **Reserve the turkey cooking liquid.**
4. **Cool both completely.**
5. **Shred the turkey finely** and check for cartilage.
6. **Combine** three parts turkey to one part rice.
7. **Moisten well** with the reserved liquid — hydration is half the point.
## Feeding through an upset stomach

1. **Small and frequent.** Four or five tiny meals beat two large ones on an irritated gut.
2. **Start at about half the usual volume** on the first day.
3. **Room temperature**, never cold from the fridge.
4. **Fresh water always available**, and make the meal soupy.
5. **Transition back** over three days once stools are normal: a quarter normal food, then half, then three-quarters.

| Day | Feeding |
|---|---|
| 1 | Half volume, split into 4–5 small meals |
| 2 | Normal volume if keeping food down |
| 3 | Begin mixing normal food back in |
| 4–5 | Complete the transition |
## Storage

- **Fridge:** 3 days · **Freezer:** 1 month in single portions
- Thaw in the fridge and warm slightly to room temperature
## Variations

- **Chicken breast** instead of turkey
- **White fish** — cod or haddock — for cats that refuse poultry
- **Plain pumpkin**, 1 tsp, added fibre that helps firm loose stools
- **Rice-free**: for a grain-sensitive cat, use plain turkey alone
## Cautions

- **Not complete nutrition.** No taurine, no vitamin premix. **Maximum three to five days**, and only with veterinary agreement.
- **Diarrhoea lasting more than 48 hours** needs investigation.
- **Never add** salt, stock, butter, milk, onion or garlic.
- **Not for diabetic cats** without veterinary input — the rice affects blood glucose.
- **Kittens dehydrate fast.** Any digestive upset in a kitten is a vet call, not a recipe.
*Complementary food only, for short-term supportive use. Speak to your vet before and during any episode of vomiting or diarrhoea.*

name: White Fish & Sweet Potato Mash
description: Soft, low-fat mash of poached white fish and sweet potato. Easy to eat and gentle on digestion.
body: *Lean, mild and soft enough for a cat with a sore mouth.*

![A cooked fish fillet plated](https://storage.googleapis.com/yucat-d8fb5.firebasestorage.app/recipes/white-fish-and-sweet-potato-mash.jpeg)
*Cod, haddock or plaice. Skinless, boneless, and checked twice.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Makes** | 4 servings |
| **Prep / Cook** | 10 min / 25 min |
| **Difficulty** | Easy |
| **Keeps** | 2 days chilled, 1 month frozen |
## Ingredients

- **200 g white fish fillet** — cod, haddock or plaice
- **60 g sweet potato**, peeled
- **3–4 tbsp of the fish poaching liquid**
White fish is one of the leanest proteins available and among the mildest in flavour, which suits cats recovering from illness.
## Method

1. **Boil the sweet potato** in unsalted water, 15–18 minutes, until it collapses under a fork.
2. **Poach the fish** separately in unsalted water, 8–10 minutes, until it flakes.
3. **Reserve the fish liquid** and cool everything completely.
4. **Check the fish for bones — twice.** Flake it apart with your fingers and run a fingertip through every piece. White fish bones are fine, translucent and easy to miss.
5. **Mash the sweet potato** smooth.
6. **Combine** roughly three parts fish to one part sweet potato.
7. **Loosen with the poaching liquid** to a soft, spoonable mash.
## Who it suits

- **Cats with dental disease** or missing teeth, since nothing needs chewing
- **Recovering cats** that need bland, easily digested food
- **Cats needing moisture**, because it carries a lot of water
- **Fussy eaters**, since white fish is mild rather than overpowering
## Portioning

| Cat weight | As a topper | As an occasional meal |
|---|---|---|
| 3 kg | 1 tsp | 60 g |
| 4 kg | 1½ tsp | 80 g |
| 5–6 kg | 1 tbsp | 100 g |
As with every recipe here, this is **complementary food**. It has no taurine supplement or vitamin premix, so it tops up a complete diet rather than replacing it.
## Storage

- **Fridge:** 2 days — fish spoils faster than poultry, so this is shorter than the other meals
- **Freezer:** 1 month, portioned in an ice-cube tray then bagged
- **Thaw in the fridge**, never on the counter
## Variations

- **Plain pumpkin** in place of sweet potato, for fewer calories
- **Extra soupy** for a cat needing hydration: double the poaching liquid
- **Fish-free**: poached chicken breast with the same method
## Cautions

- **Bones are the real risk.** Check by hand, and buy fillet rather than steaks.
- **Never raw fish** in quantity — thiaminase in some species destroys vitamin B1.
- **Fish two or three times a week at most**, to avoid fixation and nutritional imbalance.
- **Skip** for cats with a fish allergy.
- **Ask your vet** before feeding to cats with kidney disease — fish is relatively high in phosphorus.
*A supplement to a complete diet, not a replacement for it.*

name: Beef & Liver Pâté
description: A rich, iron-heavy pâté of lean beef and a little liver. Strictly portioned for vitamin A.
body: *The richest recipe in this collection, and the one with the tightest portion limit.*

![Raw meat on a wooden board](https://storage.googleapis.com/yucat-d8fb5.firebasestorage.app/recipes/beef-and-liver-pate.jpeg)
*Lean beef with a small amount of liver — the ratio is the recipe.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Makes** | About 10 tablespoon servings |
| **Prep / Cook** | 10 min / 25 min |
| **Difficulty** | Medium |
| **Keeps** | 3 days chilled, 1 month frozen |
## The ratio is the safety rule

- **200 g lean beef** — around 90% of the meat
- **25 g liver** — around 10%, and no more

Liver is exceptionally rich in **preformed vitamin A**, which cats store in the body rather than excreting. Sustained excess causes **hypervitaminosis A**, producing painful bony growths along the spine and joints that fuse over time.
> Ten percent liver is the working limit. This is one recipe where doubling an ingredient because the cat likes it causes real harm.
## Ingredients

- **200 g lean beef**, such as trimmed braising steak
- **25 g beef or chicken liver**
- **3–4 tbsp of the cooking water**
- **1 tsp plain pumpkin purée** *(optional, for texture)*
## Method

1. **Trim every scrap of visible fat** from the beef. Fat is what makes this recipe a pancreatitis risk.
2. **Simmer the beef** in unsalted water for 20–25 minutes, until tender throughout.
3. **Add the liver for the final 8 minutes**, so it firms without overcooking.
4. **Reserve 4 tbsp of the cooking liquid** and cool everything completely.
5. **Blend the beef** first, with 2 tbsp of the liquid, to a coarse paste.
6. **Add the liver** and blend to a smooth pâté.
7. **Adjust with the remaining liquid** until it falls slowly off a spoon. Stir the pumpkin through if using.
## Portioning
Smaller portions than the chicken pâté, because of the liver.

| Cat weight | Per serving | Days per week |
|---|---|---|
| 3 kg | 1 tsp | 2–3 |
| 4 kg | 1½ tsp | 2–3 |
| 5–6 kg | 1 tbsp | 2–3 |
Keep it to a few days a week and it stays comfortably within safe vitamin A intake.
## Storage

- **Fridge:** 3 days sealed
- **Freezer:** 1 month — freeze in an ice-cube tray, then bag the cubes
- **Thaw overnight in the fridge.** Never microwave, which creates burning hot spots
## Variations

- **Chicken or turkey** in place of beef, with the same 10% liver ratio
- **Liver-free** for pregnant cats or those already on a liver-rich diet — still a good pâté
- **Softer** for older cats: add more cooking liquid to a gravy consistency
## Cautions

- **Never exceed 10% liver.** This is the single most important line in the recipe.
- **Avoid entirely for pregnant cats.** Excess vitamin A causes birth defects.
- **Not for cats already eating a liver-based food** without checking with your vet.
- **Trim the fat properly.** Fatty meat is a pancreatitis risk in cats.
- **Not a complete meal** — no taurine supplement, no vitamin premix.
- **Ask your vet** before feeding to cats with kidney or liver disease.
*A treat, not a meal. Complementary food does not replace a complete and balanced diet.*

name: Egg & Chicken Scramble
description: A quick, soft scramble of egg and poached chicken. The fastest recipe here, ready in fifteen minutes.
body: *Fifteen minutes, two ingredients, no special shopping. The recipe for a cat that has gone off its food this evening.*

![An egg cooking in a pan](https://storage.googleapis.com/yucat-d8fb5.firebasestorage.app/recipes/egg-and-chicken-scramble.jpeg)
*No butter, no oil, no salt. A dry non-stick pan is all it takes.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Makes** | 2–3 servings |
| **Prep / Cook** | 5 min / 10 min |
| **Difficulty** | Easy |
| **Keeps** | 2 days chilled — do not freeze |
## Why egg works
Egg is one of the most **highly digestible** proteins available, with an amino acid profile close to ideal. It is soft, mild and easy to eat, and most cats accept it readily.
The one rule: **it must be cooked**. Raw egg white contains **avidin**, which binds biotin and causes deficiency over time, and raw egg carries a salmonella risk. Cooking solves both.
## Ingredients

- **1 medium egg**
- **60 g cooked chicken breast**, shredded
- **1 tbsp water** *(makes the scramble softer)*
> No butter, oil, milk, cream, cheese or salt. Milk and cheese cause diarrhoea in most adult cats, and there is no reason to add fat here.
## Method

1. **Poach the chicken** if you have none ready — 15 minutes in unsalted water — and cool it.
2. **Beat the egg** with the tablespoon of water.
3. **Heat a non-stick pan** over low heat. Low, not medium: high heat makes egg rubbery.
4. **Pour in the egg** and stir constantly with a spatula.
5. **Cook until completely set** — no wet or glossy patches anywhere. Firm is what you want.
6. **Remove from the heat** and fold the shredded chicken through.
7. **Cool to room temperature** before serving. Always.
## Portioning
Egg is nutrient-dense, so portions stay modest.

| Cat weight | As a treat | Frequency |
|---|---|---|
| 3 kg | 1 tbsp | 2–3 times a week |
| 4 kg | 1½ tbsp | 2–3 times a week |
| 5–6 kg | 2 tbsp | 2–3 times a week |
A whole egg is a substantial share of a small cat's daily calories, which is why one egg makes several servings.
## Storage

- **Fridge:** 2 days in a sealed container
- **Do not freeze.** Scrambled egg turns watery and rubbery on thawing
- Serve at room temperature, never straight from the fridge
## Variations

- **Egg white only** for a lower-fat version, cooked the same way
- **Turkey** instead of chicken
- **Extra soft** for older cats: add a second tablespoon of water and cook lower and slower
- **With a pinch of catnip** folded through at the end for a fussy eater
## Cautions

- **Always cooked, never raw or runny.** Avidin and salmonella are both real.
- **No shell**, which is sometimes suggested as a calcium source and is a genuine choking and cut risk.
- **No dairy** of any kind.
- **Not a complete meal** — no taurine supplement, no vitamin premix.
- **Introduce slowly.** Egg allergy exists in cats, though it is uncommon.
- **Ask your vet** before feeding to cats with kidney disease or pancreatitis.
*A treat, not a meal. Complementary food does not replace a complete and balanced diet.*

name: Chicken Broth Ice Lollies
description: Frozen chicken broth on a lick-safe stick. A slow, cooling summer treat that adds water.
body: *A treat that takes a cat ten minutes to finish instead of ten seconds, and leaves it better hydrated.*

![Frozen lollies on ice](https://storage.googleapis.com/yucat-d8fb5.firebasestorage.app/recipes/chicken-broth-ice-lollies.jpeg)
*Milder than the salmon version, and usually accepted by cats that refuse fish.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Makes** | 8–10 small lollies |
| **Active time** | 20 minutes |
| **Freezing** | 5 hours minimum |
| **Keeps** | 2 months frozen |
## Ingredients

- **150 g chicken breast**, skinless and boneless
- **500 ml water**, unsalted
- **1 tbsp plain pumpkin purée** *(optional, stops shattering)*
> **No stock cubes, no bouillon, no gravy granules.** Commercial stock is heavily salted and almost always contains onion, which damages feline red blood cells.
## Method

1. **Simmer the chicken** in the 500 ml of water for 20 minutes, until cooked through.
2. **Lift the chicken out** and cool both meat and liquid completely.
3. **Strain the broth** through a fine sieve.
4. **Blend a third of the chicken** back into the broth for body and aroma. Keep the rest for another recipe.
5. **Whisk in the pumpkin** if using — it gives the lolly a softer texture that licks rather than shatters.
6. **Pour into small moulds.** Silicone moulds work best.
7. **Add the stick.** Use a **short length of cat grass, a cardboard tube segment or a silicone mould with a built-in handle** — never a wooden lolly stick, which splinters, and never anything a cat could swallow.
8. **Freeze 5 hours**, then turn out and bag.
## A safer alternative to sticks
If you are at all unsure about the stick, **do not use one**. Freeze in a small silicone mould and serve the lolly loose on a plate. Cats do not need a handle, and it removes the risk entirely.
## Serving

- **On a flat plate** or a tiled floor — this will be batted around
- **One lolly a day maximum**, counted inside the 10% treat allowance
- **Supervise** the first few times, so you can see how your cat handles it
- **Melt one over dry food** as a topper for a cat that will not lick ice
## Storage

- **Freezer:** 2 months in a sealed, labelled bag
- **Thawed broth:** 2 days in the fridge, then discard
- **Never refreeze** a thawed lolly
## Variations

- **Turkey** instead of chicken
- **Plain water lollies** for cats that already drink well
- **Softer texture:** double the pumpkin so it licks more easily
- **Cube form** in an ice-cube tray, which is the simplest version of all
## Cautions

- **Never a wooden stick.** Splintering is a real risk, and the pieces are sharp.
- **Never commercial stock.** Salt and onion are both problems.
- **Check for bone** before blending, even with boneless breast.
- **Thaw slightly** for cats with dental disease — biting hard ice can fracture a tooth.
- **Not a complete meal.** No taurine supplement, no vitamin premix.
*A treat, not a meal. Complementary food does not replace a complete and balanced diet.*

name: Frozen Tuna & Yoghurt Drops
description: Small frozen drops of tuna and plain live yoghurt. Creamy, cooling, and only for cats that tolerate dairy.
body: *Creamier than a plain ice cube, and the one recipe here that needs a tolerance test first.*

![A bowl of yoghurt with a spoon](https://storage.googleapis.com/yucat-d8fb5.firebasestorage.app/recipes/frozen-tuna-yoghurt-drops.jpeg)
*Plain, unsweetened, live yoghurt. Nothing flavoured, and never anything sugar-free.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Makes** | About 20 small drops |
| **Active time** | 15 minutes |
| **Freezing** | 4 hours |
| **Keeps** | 6 weeks frozen |
## The dairy question, first
Most adult cats are **lactose intolerant**. They lose the enzyme lactase after weaning, and milk causes diarrhoea.
Yoghurt is the partial exception: the fermentation process consumes much of the lactose, so plain live yoghurt is often tolerated in small amounts. **Often, not always.**
> **Test before you make a batch.** Offer a quarter teaspoon of plain yoghurt and wait 24 hours. Any loose stool means this recipe is not for your cat — make the salmon broth cubes instead.
## Ingredients

- **3 tbsp plain live yoghurt**, full fat, unsweetened
- **60 g tinned tuna in spring water**, drained
- **2 tbsp water**
**Never use** flavoured, sweetened, low-fat-with-sweeteners, or any "sugar-free" yoghurt. Some contain **xylitol**, which must be kept away from pets entirely.
## Method

1. **Drain the tuna hard** and mash it completely smooth.
2. **Blend the tuna with the water** to a thin paste.
3. **Fold in the yoghurt** gently. Do not over-blend, which thins it too far.
4. **Spoon small drops** onto a baking-paper-lined tray, about a teaspoon each — or use a mini silicone mould.
5. **Freeze 4 hours** until solid.
6. **Transfer to a labelled freezer bag.**
## Serving

| Cat weight | Drops per serving | Frequency |
|---|---|---|
| 3 kg | 1 | 2 times a week |
| 4 kg | 1–2 | 2 times a week |
| 5–6 kg | 2 | 2 times a week |
Twice weekly rather than daily, for two separate reasons: the dairy, and the tuna.
Serve on a flat plate and let it soften for a minute or two before offering it to an older cat.
## Storage

- **Freezer:** 6 weeks in a sealed bag
- **Do not refreeze** anything that has thawed
- Keep them separated by baking paper, or they fuse into a block
## Variations

- **Yoghurt-free**, for lactose-intolerant cats: replace it with the water from the tuna tin and freeze as cubes
- **Salmon** instead of tuna
- **Lactose-free cat milk** in place of yoghurt, which is the safest dairy-style option
## Cautions

- **Test tolerance first.** A quarter teaspoon, then 24 hours.
- **Never sugar-free yoghurt.** Xylitol is dangerous to pets.
- **Tuna twice a week at most.** Fed often it is unbalanced and cats fixate on it.
- **Skip entirely** for cats with a history of digestive upset, pancreatitis or a fish allergy.
- **Thaw slightly** for cats with dental disease.
*A treat, not a meal. Complementary food does not replace a complete and balanced diet.*

name: Frozen Pumpkin & Chicken Bites
description: Small frozen bites of chicken and pumpkin. Fibre for hairballs, moisture for everything else.
body: *The frozen version of the lick pâté, portioned into single bites so nothing is wasted.*

![A small orange pumpkin](https://storage.googleapis.com/yucat-d8fb5.firebasestorage.app/recipes/frozen-pumpkin-and-chicken-bites.jpeg)
*Plain pumpkin purée, never pie filling. The tin should list pumpkin and nothing else.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Makes** | About 14 bites |
| **Active time** | 25 minutes |
| **Freezing** | 4 hours |
| **Keeps** | 2 months frozen |
## Ingredients

- **150 g chicken breast**, skinless and boneless
- **3 tbsp plain pumpkin purée** — 100% pumpkin
- **4 tbsp of the cooking water**
> **Pie filling is not purée.** It contains sugar and often nutmeg, which is toxic to cats. Check the ingredients list, not the front of the tin.
## Method

1. **Poach the chicken** in unsalted water for 18 minutes.
2. **Reserve 4 tbsp of the cooking water** and cool everything completely.
3. **Check for cartilage** by hand.
4. **Blend the chicken** with 2 tbsp of the liquid to a coarse paste.
5. **Add the pumpkin** and blend smooth.
6. **Loosen with the remaining liquid** until it pours slowly.
7. **Spoon into a mini ice-cube tray** or small silicone mould.
8. **Freeze 4 hours**, turn out, and bag.
## Why pumpkin
Plain pumpkin is one of the few plant foods that genuinely earns a place in a cat's diet, and it is for **fibre**, not nutrition.

- **Hairballs** — fibre helps hair move through the gut rather than gathering
- **Mild constipation** — the soluble fibre softens stools
- **Mild diarrhoea** — the same fibre adds bulk, which is why it helps in both directions
- **Low calorie** — bulk without much energy, useful for a cat on a diet
More is not better. Too much pumpkin causes loose stools on its own.
## Serving

| Cat weight | Bites per day | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 3 kg | 1 | Thaw slightly for older cats |
| 4 kg | 1–2 | |
| 5–6 kg | 2 | |
Serve on a flat plate, or **thaw one and stir it through the main meal** as a fibre topper — often the more practical use.
## Storage

- **Freezer:** 2 months in a labelled bag
- **Thawed:** 2 days in the fridge, then discard
- **Never refreeze**
## Variations

- **Turkey** instead of chicken
- **Extra fibre** for a hairball-prone cat: 4 tbsp pumpkin instead of 3
- **White fish** in place of chicken
- **Softer** for dental patients: thaw fully and serve as a pâté
## Cautions

- **Plain pumpkin only.** No pie filling, no spice, no sugar.
- **Do not overdo the fibre.** Excess causes the loose stools you were trying to fix.
- **Persistent constipation or diarrhoea is a vet visit**, not a pumpkin problem.
- **Not a complete meal** — no taurine supplement, no vitamin premix.
- **Thaw slightly** for cats with dental disease.
*A treat, not a meal. Complementary food does not replace a complete and balanced diet.*

name: Frozen Catnip Water Cubes
description: The simplest recipe here: catnip-infused water, frozen. Ten minutes, two ingredients, zero calories.
body: *Almost no calories, almost no effort, and a genuinely useful way to get a cat interested in water.*

![Ice cubes set in a silicone mould](https://storage.googleapis.com/yucat-d8fb5.firebasestorage.app/recipes/frozen-catnip-water-cubes.jpeg)
*A small silicone mould gives cubes the right size to bat around.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Makes** | 12–14 cubes |
| **Active time** | 10 minutes |
| **Freezing** | 4 hours |
| **Keeps** | 3 months frozen |
## Ingredients

- **400 ml water**
- **2 tsp dried catnip**, or a small handful of fresh leaves
That is genuinely all. These are the only treats in this collection with essentially no calorie cost, which makes them the ones you can use daily.
## Method

1. **Boil the water** and pour it over the catnip in a heatproof jug.
2. **Steep 10 minutes**, covered, like making tea. Longer makes it bitter and cats notice.
3. **Strain out the leaves** through a fine sieve, pressing gently.
4. **Cool completely** to room temperature.
5. **Pour into an ice-cube tray** and freeze for at least 4 hours.
6. **Turn out and bag**, or simply leave them in the tray.
## The point of them

This is a **hydration tool disguised as a toy**. Cats have a weak thirst drive inherited from desert ancestors, and chronic mild dehydration contributes to urinary and kidney problems over a lifetime.
Three ways to use them:

- **One cube in the water bowl.** It chills and lightly scents the water, and many cats will drink noticeably more from a bowl that has something interesting in it. This is the daily use.
- **One cube on a hard floor.** A batting toy that ends in a drink. Free enrichment.
- **In a water fountain reservoir**, where the movement and the scent combine.
## About the catnip
Roughly **two thirds of cats** respond to catnip. The trait is inherited, and kittens under about three months usually show no reaction at all.
If your cat is a non-responder, try **silvervine**, which many catnip-immune cats respond to strongly. Or simply use plain water cubes, which still work as a cooling toy.
Catnip response typically lasts about ten minutes, after which cats become temporarily immune for an hour or two. Frequent exposure blunts the effect, so occasional use keeps it potent.
## Storage

- **Freezer:** 3 months, bagged and labelled
- Once thawed, discard rather than refreezing
- If they pick up freezer odours, make a fresh batch — cats are far more sensitive to this than we are
## Variations

- **Silvervine** in place of catnip for non-responders
- **Plain water cubes**, which many cats enjoy just as much
- **A drop of tuna spring water** stirred in for a stronger scent, though this adds a few calories
- **Cat grass infusion** instead of catnip
## Cautions

- **Thaw slightly** for cats with dental disease. Biting hard ice can fracture a tooth.
- **Supervise the first few times** to see how your cat handles a slippery cube.
- **Do not use catnip essential oil.** Concentrated oils are not safe for cats; use the dried or fresh herb.
- **Excess catnip** occasionally causes mild vomiting. Two teaspoons across 400 ml is a gentle dose.
*A treat, not a meal. Complementary food does not replace a complete and balanced diet.*

name: Tuna Birthday Cake
description: A small savoury cake with a mashed-potato topping. For birthdays and adoption days, shared in slivers.
body: *A cake for the cat, sized for a cat, and eaten a teaspoon at a time.*

![Small iced cakes in a row](https://storage.googleapis.com/yucat-d8fb5.firebasestorage.app/recipes/tuna-birthday-cake.jpeg)
*The "icing" is plain mashed potato. No sugar, no dairy, no decoration.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Makes** | 1 small cake, about 12 servings |
| **Prep / Bake** | 20 min / 25 min |
| **Difficulty** | Medium |
| **Keeps** | 3 days chilled, 1 month frozen |
## Ingredients

### For the cake
- **150 g tinned tuna in spring water**, drained
- **100 g cooked chicken breast**, shredded
- **1 medium egg**
- **60 g oat flour**
- **2 tbsp water**

### For the topping
- **1 medium potato**, peeled and boiled
- **2–3 tbsp of the chicken cooking water**
> No sugar, no butter, no milk, no cream cheese, no frosting, no decorations. Everything on this cake has to be food a cat can actually eat.
## Method

1. **Heat the oven** to 180 °C (160 °C fan). Line a small round tin, about 10 cm, or use a large ramekin.
2. **Drain the tuna hard** and mash it smooth.
3. **Combine** the tuna, shredded chicken, egg and water.
4. **Fold in the oat flour** to a thick, spoonable batter.
5. **Press into the tin**, levelling the top.
6. **Bake 22–25 minutes**, until firm and a skewer comes out clean.
7. **Cool completely in the tin**, then turn out. Warm cake falls apart.
8. **Boil the potato** in unsalted water until soft, then mash with the chicken water until smooth and spreadable.
9. **Spread the potato over the cooled cake.** A piping bag makes it look like icing if you want the photograph.
10. **Chill 30 minutes** before serving so it sets.
## Serving
This is a celebration, not a meal. **One thin sliver**, roughly a teaspoon, is a serving.

| Cat weight | Serving on the day |
|---|---|
| 3 kg | 1 tsp |
| 4 kg | 1½ tsp |
| 5–6 kg | 1 tbsp |
Reduce the day's main meal slightly to compensate. Freeze the rest in portions — a whole cake is far more than one cat should eat in a week.
**Never light a candle near a cat.** Whiskers and fur catch quickly, and the cat will investigate.
## Storage

- **Fridge:** 3 days in a sealed container
- **Freezer:** 1 month, sliced and separated by baking paper
- Thaw single portions in the fridge overnight
## Variations

- **Salmon** instead of tuna
- **Sweet potato topping** in place of potato, for a little more colour
- **Layered version:** slice the cooled cake horizontally and spread pâté in the middle
- **Individual cupcakes** in a silicone mini-muffin tray, baked 15 minutes
## Cautions

- **Raw potato is not safe.** Green parts and sprouts contain solanine. Peel it, and boil it fully.
- **No dairy topping.** Cream cheese and whipped cream cause diarrhoea in most adult cats.
- **Fish twice or three times a week at most.**
- **Not a complete meal** — no taurine supplement, no vitamin premix.
- **Guest cats have different diets.** Check before sharing at a party.
*A treat, not a meal. Complementary food does not replace a complete and balanced diet.*

name: Gotcha Day Chicken Loaf
description: A firm, sliceable chicken and pumpkin loaf. Bakes once, portions into a fortnight of treats.
body: *Bake once on a Sunday and portion it into a fortnight of treats. The most practical recipe in this collection.*

![A baked loaf on a tray](https://storage.googleapis.com/yucat-d8fb5.firebasestorage.app/recipes/gotcha-day-chicken-loaf.jpeg)
*Firm enough to slice cleanly once fully cooled.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Makes** | 1 small loaf, about 20 servings |
| **Prep / Bake** | 15 min / 35 min |
| **Difficulty** | Medium |
| **Keeps** | 4 days chilled, 2 months frozen |
## Ingredients

- **300 g chicken breast**, skinless and boneless, raw and diced
- **2 medium eggs**
- **50 g oat flour**
- **3 tbsp plain pumpkin purée** — 100% pumpkin
- **1 tbsp salmon oil** *(optional)*
The chicken goes in **raw** here, unlike the other recipes. It cooks fully in the loaf, and the texture is better for it.
## Method

1. **Heat the oven** to 180 °C (160 °C fan). Line a small loaf tin, about 15 × 8 cm.
2. **Blend the raw chicken** to a coarse paste in a food processor.
3. **Add the eggs** and blend briefly to combine.
4. **Add the pumpkin** and pulse.
5. **Fold in the oat flour** by hand to a thick batter.
6. **Press into the tin** and level the surface.
7. **Bake 30–35 minutes.** It is done when the centre is firm and a skewer comes out clean and hot to the touch.
8. **Cool completely in the tin** — at least an hour. Slicing it warm will crumble it.
9. **Turn out and slice** into roughly 1 cm slices, then cut each into treat-sized cubes.
10. **Stir the salmon oil** over the cubes at the end if using, rather than baking it in.
## Getting it fully cooked
Because the chicken starts raw, the centre must reach a safe temperature. Two checks:

- The **skewer comes out hot**, not just clean
- The centre is **opaque and firm**, with no translucent or glossy patches
If in doubt, give it another 5 minutes. An underbaked loaf is a salmonella risk, and the texture is unpleasant anyway.
## Portioning

| Cat weight | Treat allowance | Cubes per day |
|---|---|---|
| 3 kg | 16 kcal | 1–2 |
| 4 kg | 20 kcal | 2 |
| 5–6 kg | 24–27 kcal | 2–3 |
One loaf is roughly a fortnight of treats for one cat, which is exactly the point of making it.
## Storage

- **Fridge:** 4 days in a sealed container
- **Freezer:** 2 months — freeze the cubes flat on a tray first, then bag them so they stay separate
- Thaw a day's worth in the fridge overnight
## Variations

- **Turkey** instead of chicken
- **Fish version:** replace 100 g of the chicken with drained tinned salmon
- **Softer loaf** for older cats: add 2 tbsp water to the batter
- **Mini loaves** in a muffin tray, baked 20 minutes, which portion themselves
## Cautions

- **Bake it through.** Raw chicken in the mix means the centre must be fully cooked.
- **Cool completely before slicing**, or it crumbles.
- **Not a complete meal** — no taurine supplement, no vitamin premix.
- **Introduce slowly** if your cat has a sensitive stomach.
- **Ask your vet** before feeding to cats with kidney disease or pancreatitis.
*A treat, not a meal. Complementary food does not replace a complete and balanced diet.*

name: Dental Crunch Sticks
description: Hard, thin chicken sticks baked twice for a real snap. A small mechanical extra, never a substitute for brushing.
body: *Baked twice, like biscotti, so they are genuinely hard rather than merely crisp.*

![Dough being cut into shapes on a board](https://storage.googleapis.com/yucat-d8fb5.firebasestorage.app/recipes/dental-crunch-sticks.jpeg)
*Cut into thin sticks so the cat has to chew rather than swallow whole.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Makes** | About 30 sticks |
| **Prep / Bake** | 15 min / 25 min total |
| **Difficulty** | Medium |
| **Keeps** | 3 weeks airtight, 3 months frozen |
## Set expectations honestly
**Brushing is the only measure with strong evidence behind it.** Daily brushing is the gold standard, and no treat replaces it.

What a hard, chewed treat can do is provide a little mechanical action at the tooth surface. It is a small extra, worth having, and it does nothing about the area under the gum line where periodontal disease actually starts.
> Ordinary dry food does not clean teeth — standard kibble shatters on contact, above the gum line. These are harder and shaped to be chewed, which is the difference.
## Ingredients

- **200 g chicken breast**, skinless and boneless
- **140 g oat flour**
- **1 medium egg white**
- **1 tsp dried parsley** *(optional)*
- **1–2 tbsp of the cooking water**
The egg white rather than a whole egg keeps them hard. Yolk adds fat, and fat makes them softer.
## Method

1. **Poach the chicken** in unsalted water for 18 minutes, then cool completely. Reserve the liquid.
2. **Blend to a fine paste** with 1 tbsp of the cooking water.
3. **Mix in the egg white** and the parsley.
4. **Work in the oat flour** to a stiff dough. It should be noticeably firmer than a biscuit dough.
5. **Heat the oven** to 170 °C (150 °C fan) and line a tray.
6. **Roll to 4 mm** and cut into sticks about **1 cm × 4 cm**.
7. **First bake: 15 minutes.**
8. **Turn every stick over** and **bake again for 10 minutes**.
9. **Turn the oven off and leave them inside** with the door closed for 30 minutes. This is what drives out the last of the moisture.
10. **Cool completely** on a rack.
They should snap cleanly. If any bend, return them to a 150 °C oven for 5 more minutes.
## Serving safely

- **One or two a day**, inside the 10% treat allowance
- **Supervise**, especially at first
- **Break in half** for small cats or fast eaters
- **Do not give to a cat with known dental disease or a loose tooth.** A hard treat on a painful mouth is cruel and can fracture a tooth. Use the pâté or the fish mash instead

| Cat weight | Sticks per day |
|---|---|
| 3 kg | 1 |
| 4 kg | 1–2 |
| 5–6 kg | 2 |
## Storage

- **Airtight jar:** 3 weeks — the longest here, because they are genuinely dry
- **Freezer:** 3 months
- If they soften, refresh at 150 °C for 8 minutes and cool completely
## Variations

- **Turkey** instead of chicken
- **Fish version:** drained tinned sardines in place of half the chicken
- **Softer, for younger cats:** skip the second bake
- **Parsley-free**, which suits cats on restricted diets
## Cautions

- **This is not a replacement for brushing.** Nothing is.
- **Not for cats with existing dental disease**, loose teeth or a history of tooth fracture.
- **Supervise every time.** Hard treats are a choking risk if bolted.
- **Parsley in small amounts only**, and never spring parsley, which is toxic to cats.
- **If your cat swallows them whole**, this recipe is not achieving anything — go back to brushing.
*A treat, not a meal. Complementary food does not replace a complete and balanced diet. Ask your vet to check your cat's teeth at every visit.*
